extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and authors working with Springer Nature journals (and internal Springer Nature editorial staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level guidance and standards for maintaining research integrity across Springer Nature journals, covering prevention, investigation/resolution of concerns, reproducibility, data/code sharing, peer review transparency, COPE-aligned practices, and DEI considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes of Conduct for Editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes of Conduct set the standards and expectations for all Springer Nature Editors (internal and external). These are based on guidelines and best practice recommendations issued by organizations such as the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature provides robust training and resources to maintain the highest standards of editorial practice; Editors are expected to follow the Codes of Conduct and associated training materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling allegations of misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how allegations of misconduct should be handled (part of COPE's Core Practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE's Core Practices set out clear guidance including step-by-step flowcharts and practical support for dealing with allegations; Springer Nature's Resolutions team investigates concerns and can take actions after investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and contributorship policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on authorship and contributorship (listed as a core practice area by COPE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and journals should have clear policies defining authorship/contributorship and follow COPE guidance and flowcharts where disputes arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability and data sharing policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on data availability are a core practice: promoting standardised data sharing policies and support for protocol sharing to advance reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature provides a Research Data Helpdesk, standardised data policies, and actively promotes benefits of sharing research data; journals are expected to implement and enforce data availability statements and data sharing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review process and ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for the peer review process and ethical conduct of peer review (part of COPE's Core Practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes support for multiple models of peer review, transparent peer review options, and training/resources for editors to ensure ethical peer review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints and appeals procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes for complaints and appeals are part of COPE's Core Practices and should be in place for journals/publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should have documented procedures for receiving and handling complaints and appeals in line with COPE guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing conflict of interest / competing interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and procedures for managing conflict of interest / competing interest (identified in COPE's Core Practices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and journals should require disclosure of competing interests and manage them according to COPE recommendations and publisher policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal management standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal management (editorial governance and operational standards) is named as a core practice area by COPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes expectations around editorial board roles, selection, and governance consistent with COPE/core practice guidance and Springer Nature Codes of Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication discussion, corrections and corrections processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes for post-publication discussion and corrections — including handling honest errors, author disputes, and potential misconduct (CORE practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature's Resolutions team investigates post-publication concerns; resources include videos/transcripts explaining investigations and actions that may be taken (corrections, expressions of concern, retractions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of COPE guides and flowcharts
rubrics_metrics.description: COPE publishes guides and flowcharts offering step-by-step practical support on handling different aspects of publication best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are expected to consult COPE flowcharts and guides when resolving integrity issues; Springer Nature works closely with COPE to develop educational resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and open research practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility is a foundation of robust research; publisher commitment to advancing reproducibility through editorial policies, publishing infrastructure and partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes promoting protocol sharing, introducing standardised data sharing policies, and participating in frameworks (e.g., MDAR) that harmonise reporting to improve reproducibility and replicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data support and incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and incentives for data sharing, including provision of a Research Data Helpdesk and standardised data policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature actively promotes benefits of data sharing to researchers and provides infrastructure and guidance to help authors comply with data policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review and publication of code / software
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals encourage researchers whose papers rely on bespoke software to provide the programs for peer review; a code and software submission checklist is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit code/software for peer review following the publisher's checklist to aid reproducibility and enable reviewers to assess computational work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of the MDAR Framework (Minimal Standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation in development of the MDAR Framework — a harmonised approach to transparent reporting in the life sciences covering aspects essential for reproducibility, replicability and open research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals/authors are encouraged to align reporting with MDAR's minimum standards for materials, design, analysis and reporting to improve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in peer review and preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for opening up the 'black box' of peer review, supporting preprint deposition and citation, and offering multiple models of peer review (e.g., In Review; Transparent Peer Review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options include permitting preprints, enabling manuscript tracking (In Review), and publishing peer reviewer reports and authors' responses alongside articles where journals offer Transparent Peer Review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for TOP guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for the Transparency and Openness Promotion (TOP) guidelines to implement better, more transparent research practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals are encouraged to implement TOP guideline elements appropriate to their discipline to improve openness and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention through training, tools and proactive investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of robust training and resources to maintain high editorial standards and proactive investigation of patterns of research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature provides training for internal and external editors, implements tools and processes to recognise misconduct, and proactively investigates patterns of malpractice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolutions team process for post-publication concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated Resolutions team handles reported issues across Springer Nature that require research integrity expertise and can investigate complex cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Resolutions team investigates concerns (from honest errors to possible misconduct), advises on actions to make the publication record reliable, and provides explanatory materials (videos and transcripts) about their workflows and potential outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: DEI Recruitment Frameworks for editorial boards and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Frameworks and initiatives to increase diversity among commissioned authors, peer reviewers and editorial boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature provides DEI Recruitment Frameworks for Editorial Board Members and reviewers as part of broader ethics and recruitment practices.
